Directions: Use the information about rattlesnake rattles and your knowledge of science to answer each question that follows.
Title: Rattlesnake Rattles
Content: Sammy saw a rattlesnake at the zoo. Picture `1` shows a rattlesnake.
Sammy wanted to learn more about rattlesnakes. She read that:

:ibox:• Rattles are hollow pieces that are joined together. They are made of the same material as the snake's scales.
• A rattlesnake shakes its tail to warn predators that the snake will attack.
• The rattling noise is made when the snake holds its tail straight up and shakes it. The pieces hit `text(one)` another and make a buzzing sound.
• When a rattlesnake grows, it sheds its skin. A new rattle is added each time.
• The rattles on a snake may break off. The rattles grow back `text(one)` piece at a time.

Sammy read a news article that said some groups of rattlesnakes do not have fully developed rattles. Instead, they have curled tails with a rattle that cannot make a rattling sound. She made a table to show what she learned.
